key_cases.case_name: Kenosha County DHS v. Jodie W.
key_cases.holding: Terminating an incarcerated parent's rights under the continuing-CHIPS ground because she failed to meet a condition of return she could not possibly satisfy while imprisoned, without regard to her actual parenting or the child's condition, violates substantive due process.
key_cases.relevance: It is Wisconsin's leading authority that treating a parent's status - incarceration - as a proxy for unfitness is unconstitutional.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court improperly deemed Jodie unfit solely by virtue of her status as an incarcerated person without regard for her actual parenting activities or the condition of her child

key_cases.case_name: Monroe County DHS v. Kelli B.
key_cases.holding: The incestuous-parenthood ground for termination, applied to a mother who was herself the child victim of the incest, is not narrowly tailored to a compelling state interest and violates her substantive due process right to parent.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Wisconsin precedent for challenging a termination ground that penalizes a parent for a status or circumstance rather than conduct.
key_cases.quote: Because we determine that the statute, as applied, is not narrowly tailored to advance a compelling state interest, we conclude that it violates Kelli's right to substantive due process.

key_cases.case_name: Monroe County DHS v. Luis R.
key_cases.holding: ICWA sec. 1912(f) applies in a TPR even though the Indian child was already placed outside the parental home, and a county social worker without expertise beyond ordinary social-work qualifications is not a 'qualified expert witness'; sec. 1912(d) carries no beyond-a-reasonable-doubt burden.
key_cases.relevance: Failure to apply ICWA's protections to an Indian family is a reversible, rights-based failure in Wisconsin.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that 25 U.S.C. § 1912 (f) applies even though the child has been placed outside the parental home before the TPR proceeding is filed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: ICWA sec. 1912(f)'s heightened showing does not apply where the parent never had legal or physical custody of the Indian child, and sec. 1912(d)'s remedial-and-rehabilitative-efforts requirement applies only where terminating the parent's rights would precipitate the breakup of an Indian family.
key_cases.relevance: Any claim that ICWA's protections were denied to an Indian family must now be framed within the custody and family-breakup limits this decision imposes.
key_cases.quote: we hold that §1912(d) applies only in cases where an Indian family's "breakup" would be precipitated by the termination of the parent's rights.
